title: Things to Do in Rome: Three Stops for a Closer Look
description: Explore Piazza Navona, Ponte Sisto and Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere on a Rome outing built around public spaces and a closer look.
body:
For things to do in Rome between the major ticketed sights, give the city’s public spaces their own afternoon. Piazza Navona, Ponte Sisto and Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere take you from a broad square to a river crossing and into a neighbourhood setting.

This is an invitation to spend more time with fewer places. You can enjoy the outing without adding a museum entry, a guided tour or a reservation at every stop.

1. Give Piazza Navona room to unfold

Piazza Navona’s elongated shape and fountains make it a place to appreciate as a whole, rather than a single object to photograph. Turismo Roma’s square guide explains its history and monuments.

Find an open place on the public square and enjoy the relationship between its buildings, water and movement. The view can change simply because the people around you change. There is no need to secure a café table before you can spend time here.

Plan the stop: Public-square viewing is separate from paid interiors and nearby attractions. Follow current restrictions around fountains and events. Stay outside fountain basins and keep the routes through the square clear.

2. Cross the Tiber at Ponte Sisto

Ponte Sisto connects the city near Via dei Pettinari with the Trastevere side at Piazza Trilussa. The bridge is described in Turismo Roma’s official guide.

Allow the crossing to be part of the afternoon rather than a gap between attractions. From the pedestrian route, the river offers a different scale from the streets you have just left. You can enjoy it without descending to the lower riverbank or planning a boat trip.

Plan the stop: Leave room for people crossing and stop only where it is comfortable and safe. Use the bridge and upper public streets; lower riverside paths may have different access conditions.

3. Look at Santa Maria in Trastevere from the square

At Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere, the basilica’s façade forms one side of a lively public space. The city’s basilica guide provides context for the building and its decoration.

Let the square be the destination for a while. You can appreciate the façade from public space and enjoy the setting without treating the church as another interior to complete. It is a particularly useful stop when your group wants a shared pause after moving through the city.

Plan the stop: This suggestion stays outside. If you choose to enter the basilica, check current visiting arrangements, dress appropriately and respect worship. Services and visitor access are different things.

Allow time between the squares

Start at Piazza Navona, make your way to Ponte Sisto using public streets, then continue from Piazza Trilussa to Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere. Budget around three hours for a relaxed outing with pauses. Add more for a meal or any interior visit.

Use a current map for the connections and consider the uneven paving, crowds and street crossings that can affect pace. The three suggested exterior stops need no attraction ticket. Food, transport and optional visits are separate. You can shorten the plan to the bridge and Trastevere if you already spent the morning sightseeing.

Take part in the visit

SideQuest’s Rome City Edition includes activities at these places, offering playful ways to engage with the city around you. The prompts stay in the app so the discoveries still belong to your day. Download SideQuest and look for Rome when you are ready to explore.
